transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, I hope I'm in the right place for this, but what brings me in is... I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I don't want to make a big fuss out of it, and maybe it's just me being a little scatterbrained, but it's getting a bit frustrating. I'm a carpenter, and lately, just one saw starting up in the shop, or somebody walking past the office, or even just a thought popping up about another job... it'll completely pull me off what I’m doing. 

And then before I know it, the whole day just gets away from me. I try so hard to stay on track, I really do, but it's like I just lose the thread. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not wasting your time with this.
Has this trouble concentrating been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this a new problem that started more recently?

Oh, um... well, if I'm being completely honest, I suppose it's not exactly a new thing. I really hate to sound like I'm just making excuses for myself, you know? But... even way back in grade school, definitely before I was twelve, my teachers were always telling my mother that I was bright but careless. 

I was always losing my homework, or I'd completely forget the instructions they had just given the class. I'd end up just staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. I always just thought I was a bit of a daydreamer, I guess, and I tried not to let it be a bother to anyone. Is... is that the sort of thing you were looking to know?
Aside from getting distracted, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about different things—like work, health, or family—more days than not, and having trouble controlling that worry?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I mean, everybody gets a little stressed now and then, right? But I don't sit around fretting about my health or my family or anything like that. I try to look on the bright side of things. I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm some sort of nervous wreck. I just... I just have a hard time keeping my thoughts in a straight line sometimes. Does that answer your question okay?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or noticing that you've lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

No, no, nothing like that. I'm generally a pretty upbeat person, I think. I mean, sure, it gets a little frustrating when I mess up a measurement at the shop because I wasn't paying attention, but I don't let it get me down for long. I still love woodworking and being out in the shop just as much as I always have. I'm definitely not depressed or anything, if that's what you're asking. I really hope I'm being helpful... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
